title: ASP.NET Web API Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: A controller action handles a route. HttpGet maps GET /hello to the method. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: AddControllers registers controller services and MapControllers uses their route attributes. Hello returns text. AddControllers and MapControllers are both needed.

exercises.question: Ok creates a successful response with data. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Ok wraps the anonymous object in a 200 response, and the web formatter writes JSON. Return data objects so the framework serialises them.

exercises.question: FromRoute reads a path value. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: FromRoute reads the constrained n value. The method doubles the resulting 4. A route constraint controls matching; it is not a full data validation policy.

exercises.question: FromQuery makes the source of an input clear. GET /page with no n uses 1. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: FromQuery uses the URL input when present; otherwise the default parameter is 1. Inputs from clients still need suitable limits.

exercises.question: FromBody reads a JSON request body. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The JSON title is bound to the record. Ok returns that typed value as JSON. Send the correct Content-Type so JSON can be parsed.

exercises.question: ApiController checks validation attributes. A valid POST /books with {"title":"Moon Trip"} reaches this action. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The required attribute is checked before the action. A valid title reaches Ok; an absent title gives 400. Required checks presence; add more rules for your actual needs.

exercises.question: CreatedAtAction sends status 201 and a link to the new item. Send POST /books with {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: CreatedAtAction uses ById and id 1 to build a location. The submitted book is its response body. The named action and route values must identify a real route.

exercises.question: NotFound creates a 404 result. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: NotFound chooses status 404 and serialises the supplied error field. A missing item should not look like a successful response.

exercises.question: A collection becomes a JSON array. Open GET /books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The two strings become the two items in a JSON array. Use a clear item shape for larger collections.

exercises.question: A controller can set response metadata before returning a result. Open GET /note. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The action sets its header before calling Ok. The body still contains only the note field. Headers must be set before the response starts.

exercises.question: NoContent returns status 204. Send DELETE /books/1 for this practice response. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: NoContent selects 204 and sends no resource body. This sample only shows the response; it has no stored book to delete.

exercises.question: IActionResult allows different outcomes. GET /score/8 returns a success; a negative score returns 400. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The positive route number bypasses BadRequest. The success branch returns score 8. Check invalid input before returning a success result.
